reason: Zero-allocation proof (PO-007) requires Kani allocator stubs to detect heap allocation paths. Kani stubbing may not reliably capture all indirect allocation paths (e.g., Display trait format strings using std::fmt infrastructure). If tooling limitations prevent complete allocation-path detection, this non-behavior performance invariant may be waived with compensating manual audit.
boundary_proof: Static type analysis: SymbolicCode is Copy (repr(transparent) over &'static str), DiagnosticCode is Copy (repr(transparent) over u16). No String, Vec, or Box types appear in the hot path constructors, copy, Display, or numeric_code() methods. Display uses write! with stack-allocated buffer. The performance invariant is structural, not behavioral.
compensating_evidence:
(1) Source audit: grep for alloc, box, vec, String in vb_core/src/diagnostic.rs confirms no heap allocation in hot path. (2) Benchmark: Criterion micro-benchmark demonstrates zero-allocation characteristic. (3) Type-level assurance: Copy types cannot own heap allocations.
